title: Shared atoms of the core-internal contract
description: Referenced by the other core-internal schemas; validates nothing on its own. Identifiers, amounts, timestamps, nodes and denominations are the provider-role contract's, and digests and names the module interface's, by reference.

token.description: A reason or a bound's name, as the component that gives it names it: a lower-case word or words joined by _.

count.description: A count of one or more, no larger than 2^53 - 1.

role.description: The role an actor acts in, each recorded apart even where one party holds several (REQ-AUD-8): a customer (requester, payer or beneficiary), the operator, a provider, a verifier, a regulator or a checker by an identified permission (REQ-AUZ-7), or one of Core's own parts acting on its own account. An agent acts in its party's role (REQ-OPS-5).

actor_kind.description: What kind of actor acts: a person, an agent acting for its accountable party within the scope that party set (REQ-AUZ-8), or a component (a module, a reserve's system, one of Core's parts). Humans and agents use one contract, and the record says which acted (REQ-OPS-5, REQ-ORD-10).

decided.description: A decision a later call carries out.

expires_at.description: When it ends, by Core's clock: after the request's at, and no later than its until.

actor.description: Who acts. Both identifiers are references, never an identity itself (REQ-AUD-6).

party.description: The accountable party it acts for: where limits bind and where actors are compared (REQ-AUZ-8, ADR-0011).

acts.description: The actor, as external authentication established it (REQ-AUZ-1).

when.description: When a verified entry's action happened, and by whose clock (REQ-AUD-1).

source.description: Whose clock gave the time (REQ-AUD-1): Core's own, or the module platform's as a record it handed over states it.

stated_when.description: When a party says it made a statement (REQ-AUD-1, REQ-AUD-2).

at.description: The time the maker states, its envelope's made_at.

source.description: Always the maker's own statement, which rutent has not verified.

reserve.description: The reserve: the provider of the route's last deposit.

node.description: The outer node it deposits to.

account.description: The account or address at the reserve, by reference; one the requester provides is part of the destination too (REQ-ORD-35).

route_end.description: What a route that moves value ends at, as the action states it, so policy can hold it against the authorisation (REQ-AUZ-3).

delivers.description: The amount it is expected to deliver, in the to asset's unit, to hold against any floor.

catalogue_change.description: A change to the catalogue, each a permission of its own (REQ-AUZ-6). accept_module, revoke_release, mark_stale, declare_exploited, reinstate, withdraw_release, promote and roll_back (a staging ended with the version in force kept, ADR-0014) are about one module release, and only they name its version; grant, revoke_grant and set_slippage are about one tuple, and only they name it, save that a grant and its revocation name a verifier's class in its place (REQ-CAT-13).; set_setting sets one of the operator's settings, and only it names one (T-020-45); confirm_releases is the operator's word that a provider's releases may come back into force after the platform's unclean end (T-013-11), and only it names the versions it confirms (T-020-49). list_public_network and delist_public_network list a public network with the reader service that reads it, and delist it, and only they name a public network (DEC-28, T-020-59). The Rust types check these.

action.description: An action policy decides: one that moves value, posts a route, changes the catalogue, moves a stuck order's value, erases a kept statement, reads a private node's record or a holding account's balance (REQ-AUZ-1, REQ-AUD-13, REQ-ORD-41, REQ-AUD-15).

action_move_value.description: Handing a segment's value-moving operation to its provider.

origin_reserve.description: The order's origin reserve: the provider of its first withdrawal, or the holding account's provider on a route handed on (REQ-AUZ-9).

route.description: What the route it belongs to ends at, as it stands now.

action_post_route.description: Posting a route, which only the operator may do (REQ-AUZ-2).

decision_record.description: The digest of the recorded decision that chose the route.

suggested_by.description: Who suggested it, if anyone did; a suggestion has no standing until posted (REQ-AUZ-2).

version.description: The module release it is about.

tuple.description: The tuple it is about, where it is about one.

class.description: The class a verifier's grant, or its revocation, is for, in place of a tuple: a verifier advertises classes, not tuples (REQ-CAT-13). Never with a tuple, which the Rust types check. A grant of classes alone attributes its maker's judgements of those classes alone, in the verifier's role.

advertising_keys.description: The provider's advertising keys, at least one, each once: named exactly by a grant, which the Rust types check. The latest grant in the log replaces them, and they are the log's first trust in the provider's advertisements.

statement_key.description: The key the release's module signs its statements with: named exactly by accept_module, which the Rust types check.

setting.description: The operator's setting it sets, and its value: named exactly by set_setting, which the Rust types check. For a setting about a provider, provider is that provider; for one about the whole deployment, the deployment's operator.

versions.description: The provider's versions a confirmation of its releases puts back in force, as the platform's record holds them, at least one, each once: named exactly by confirm_releases, which the Rust types check (T-020-49).

public_network.description: The public network a listing or a delisting is about: named exactly by list_public_network, with its listing, and by delist_public_network, without one, which the Rust types check (DEC-28, T-020-59). The change's provider is then the caller's own party: the deployment operator's, or one of its desks'.

subject_name.description: The subject name a reader host's server certificate carries (its SAN, a dNSName), which Core holds the host's certificate to under the operator's CA (DEC-28): a lower-case DNS name of at least two labels, with no wildcard, no trailing dot and a last label that starts with a letter, so it names one host and is never an IP address's literal, decimal or hexadecimal.

public_network.description: A public network a listing or a delisting is about (DEC-28, T-020-59): the network, as an outer node names it, and, for a listing, what lists it.

listing.description: What lists it: present exactly for list_public_network, which the Rust types check.

network_listing.description: What lists a public network (DEC-28, ADR-0007 as amended): the network's identity, how to find its reader, who the reader is, its version and its trust rule. Its identity and trust rule are paired: a chain id is read from an RPC pool, and a genesis hash by a light client. Core checks each at start-up against the reader's own network_rules answer, and a network whose reader is unreachable or fails the check doesn't start.

identity.description: The network's identity: a genesis hash, or a chain id.

version.description: The reader's version, which Core holds each answer's to (REQ-AUD-4).

trust.description: The reader's trust rule: a light client, or a pool of RPC endpoints with a quorum of at least two.

reader_endpoint.description: How Core finds a reader (item reader-registration-path): the deployment's host setting, by name, that holds its reader host's address, and the reader's name on that host, the maker of its answers.

reader_identity.description: Who a reader is, as Core holds it (DEC-28): the SHA-256 digest of the operator's CA certificate that issues the host's server certificate, the subject name that certificate carries, and the reader's statement key. Never the host's leaf certificate, so rotating it under the same CA and name needs no listing change.

ca.description: The SHA-256 digest of the operator's CA certificate (DER): a CA's, never a leaf's.

action_ask_reversal.description: Asking the provider of a failed segment to reverse it (REQ-ORD-3, REQ-ORD-11): the segment owes its reversal, and the provider is the one that failed it.

provider.description: The provider that failed it, asked to reverse.

action_ask_status.description: Asking a segment's provider where the segment stands, late, once it failed or fell silent (REQ-ORD-1, INV-4): a decided action, taken as an effect under a fresh transaction of its order, which it names, before the question is sent, so a late status is traceable from the log (T-020-36); no entry before it names that transaction (status-is-asked-under-a-fresh-transaction). The provider is the one the segment's move went to, which the log holds (status-is-asked-of-the-segments-provider); its answer is kept as its statement and moves nothing.

transaction.description: The fresh transaction it is asked under: never the segment's own, nor one any other entry named before.

action_read_holding_balance.description: Reading a holding account's balance from the module that holds it (REQ-AUD-15, REQ-AUZ-1, T-020-63): Core's schedule asks each public node's wallet and each private node's publisher's module, a decided action taken as an effect under a fresh transaction it names, before the module is asked, so a reading is traceable from the log; no entry before it names that transaction. What the module answers is a balance and moves nothing.

node.description: The inner node whose holding account is read.

provider.description: The provider whose module holds the account, asked.

asset.description: The asset whose balance is read.

transaction.description: The fresh transaction it is asked under: no entry before it names it.

action_repeat_operation.description: Asking a segment's provider to carry out the segment's own operation again (REQ-ORD-1, REQ-CAT-10, T-020-63): where its outcome was left unknown and the provider declares no status query but a repeat safe. A decided action, taken as an effect before the operation is handed over again, since a first run the platform ended before it took effect makes the repeat that move's first carrying-out. It names the segment's own transaction.

segment.description: The segment whose operation is carried out again.

transaction.description: The segment's own transaction, which the repeat is of.

action_refile_arrival.description: Filing an arrival anew against the order it differed from (REQ-ORD-23), a decided action (T-020-52): the deployment's operator, or the reserve the arrival came to, files it, and policy decides that before the refiling entry is recorded, which cites the permit. It takes no effect.

arrival.description: The receipt of the arrival's entry.

order.description: The order it is filed against.

filer.description: Who files it anew: the request's caller.

action_erase_statement.description: Erasing a kept statement's bytes from the evidence store, a decided action: the store erases only on its effect's done result, and the commitment stays in the log (REQ-AUD-13).

commitment.description: The commitment the bytes are kept under.

reason.description: Why, as a token: a label to read, which no decision branches on.

overrides_citations.description: Whether the erasure goes ahead while later entries cite the statement: false unless set. Unset, the log refuses it while anything rests on the statement; set, it is the operator's override, a permission of its own, and the log admits the erasure only where its permitting decision's action sets it (REQ-AUD-13).

action_resolve_stuck.description: Moving a stuck order's value as its decide step named, outside the order's authorisation (REQ-AUZ-4, ADR-0011).

carries_out.description: The decide step's decision it carries out.

resolution.description: The outcome it moves, exactly as the decide step named it, the provider that moves it included; the log admits it only so.

transaction.description: The transaction the move goes under at that provider, exactly as the decide step named it: what its outcome's evidence is about, as a move_value's is about its segment.

refusal_class.description: Why policy refused, as a stable class: the actor's role or permissions don't allow it; an input the decision needs is missing (REQ-AUZ-5); it isn't inside the authorisation it names (REQ-AUZ-3); the accountable party is past its bound (REQ-OPS-1, REQ-AUZ-8, REQ-CPL-5); the actor acts for no identified accountable party (REQ-AUZ-8); or one accountable party would both decide a stuck order's outcome and move its value (REQ-AUZ-4).

not_known_cause.description: Why policy could not decide (REQ-AUZ-5); nothing moves on it.

action_accept_fault.description: The customer accepting a provider's showing that a failed segment's failure was its fault (REQ-ORD-11): a decision of policy's on the policy handle, as an order's authorisation is, asked by the order's requester in its open session and naming the showing it accepts. It takes no effect; the reversal_carrier that rests on it records who carries the reversal. The operator accepts a showing by its accept_fault command instead.

session.description: The customer's session it is asked in (REQ-ORD-32).

showing_named.description: A provider's showing of fault as an acceptance names it: the transaction its result is about, and the commitment its stated entry names its bytes by.

operator_setting.description: One of the operator's settings and its value (T-020-45): what a set_setting change sets, so policy decides each and the log holds it. The values stay the deployment's to choose.

formula.description: The operator's own fee (REQ-QTE-2, REQ-QTE-5), as the router's bounds carry it.

limit.description: A tuple's slippage limit (REQ-QTE-9), as the router's bounds carry it.

grade.description: The weakest evidence the operator accepts on the tuple (REQ-ORD-39).

listed.description: Whether the operator lists the node public.

confirmations.description: The confirmations a movement at the node waits for before Core takes it as final, where the operator sets them (DEC-13).

ceiling.description: A ceiling on value in flight at one provider (REQ-ORD-8), as the router's bounds carry it.
A ceiling on value in flight across one publisher's providers (REQ-ORD-8), as the router's bounds carry it.

job.description: One of Core's scheduled jobs, by name (T-020-48).

seconds.description: Its period, in whole seconds: zero runs it on every tick of Core's schedule (T-020-49).

provider.description: The provider whose segments left unknown are asked their status again at this cadence: named only for the status question's job, status_asks, which the Rust types check (T-020-49). The change's provider is then this provider.

cutover.description: Its cutover date, from which a statement under it is void (REQ-PRT-4).

seconds.description: How long an order filed on an automatic deposit waits for its customer to accept a quote shown without a firm rate, in whole seconds from the first quote shown (REQ-QTE-10, T-020-51).

action_read_node_record.description: Asking a private node's publisher's provider for its record of the node, for the segments of an order that pass it (REQ-ORD-41, T-020-58): a decided action, taken as an effect under a fresh transaction, which it names, before the question is put, so the read is traceable from the log. Core's closing takes it while it grades a segment and Core's tick takes it for an order still unsettled at the node. What the provider answers is taken as its statement only as the question's answer, and moves nothing.

segment.description: A segment of the order that passes the node.

node.description: The private node whose record is read.

provider.description: The provider of the node's publisher that is asked.

transaction.description: The fresh transaction the question is asked under.

about.description: The transactions the read is about: the segments whose record is asked for, at least one (the question's `about`).

by.description: Who asked: a segment's grading, or the tick's read of the publishers' records (T-020-67). Kept in the log so a reopened Core counts what each has asked.
